title: Preview proxy injects <base href="/__codeyam_preview/">, silently breaking relative links in any page served from a subdirectory
description:
Any page the preview proxy serves from a subdirectory has its relative links rewritten to the wrong URL, producing a 404 that looks like a missing file rather than a resolution bug.

What happens: the proxy injects `<base href="/__codeyam_preview/">` into every proxied document (a second `<base href>` reset appears later in the head). A document served at `/__codeyam_preview/<dir>/index.html` therefore resolves its relative hrefs against `/__codeyam_preview/` instead of against its own directory, so the `<dir>/` segment is dropped:

  document : /__codeyam_preview/__design-round-1/index.html   (200)
  href     : ./01-mockup.html
  resolves : /__codeyam_preview/01-mockup.html                 (404)
  expected : /__codeyam_preview/__design-round-1/01-mockup.html (200 when requested directly)

Confirmed by driving a real browser at the proxied index and clicking the first link: the document response is a 404 on the flattened path, while curl against the correct nested path returns 200 through the same proxy. So the file is served fine — only link resolution is wrong.

Why it bites: the assumption behind the injected base is that proxied pages are app routes served from the root, which holds for framework routes but not for static assets under public/. It affects any multi-page static bundle placed in public/ — design mockups, a coverage or bundle-analyzer report, a Storybook export, any vendored HTML doc set. There is no diagnostic: the page loads, the click lands on the app's own 404 route, and nothing distinguishes it from a genuinely missing file. Worth noting `diagnose-preview` is aimed at exactly this class of "proxy mutates the document" failure but does not currently surface the base-href rewrite.

Possible fixes, roughly in order of preference: (a) set the injected base to the requested document's own directory rather than the proxy root; (b) skip base injection entirely for responses served from the static/public directory, since those are not app routes; (c) failing either, document the constraint and have `preview-nav` warn when the target path has more than one segment and resolves into a static asset directory.

Workaround used: publish every file FLAT at the public root with a shared filename prefix, so the document's own directory and the injected base are both `/` and relative hrefs resolve identically through the proxy and on the dev server directly.

Observed on the puzzle-school-rebuild branch (Astro static site) while serving design-round mockups for Live Preview.
